editorial:
You meet Simon and Robyn, a couple settling into a new home and a fresh start. Their calm routine gets shaken when Simon bumps into Gordo, an old classmate who seems friendly but awkward. At first, the visits and gifts feel harmless, even kind. Soon, small moments turn tense, and you start wondering what Gordo really wants. The movie keeps you guessing without rushing, building a slow, uneasy mood that makes every conversation feel loaded.

The acting is strong, especially the way each character hides something behind polite smiles. The pacing is steady, with twists that land because they grow from real emotions, not cheap shocks. It can feel uncomfortable and heavy, so skip it if you want light fun. If you enjoy smart thrillers, watch it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture and sound.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Gordo reveals he knew about Simon's cruel past and uses that truth to break him. Robyn learns Simon lied and manipulated people, and their marriage falls apart. Gordo sends a video implying he may have assaulted Robyn while she was drugged, but it is unclear if it really happened. The last shot leaves Simon terrified and powerless, while Gordo walks away having won the mind game.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological thrillers with twists.
